prompt:
I need the front end for Part Practice. A small, donation-funded web app a volunteer community choir uses to share rehearsal recordings and part-learning tracks with its members between weekly practices.

Who's using it: Doreen Achebe, 58, a second-year alto in the 46-member Riverside Commons Community Choir. She reads music slowly and learns her part mostly by ear, practicing on her laptop at the kitchen table in the evenings.

What they're doing right now: The winter concert is in 19 days. At Tuesday's rehearsal the director stopped the altos three times in bars 33–48 of 'Lully, Lulla, Lullay' because they kept going flat on the descending line. Doreen is going over that passage now: playing the alto learning track slowed to about 80% speed, going back to bar 33 again and again, then switching to the full-choir recording from last Tuesday to hear how her line fits against the sopranos. When she is comfortable she wants to move on to the next piece in concert order, 'In the Bleak Midwinter', where she last stopped at 1:42.

What's in the system at this point: Winter concert program: 9 pieces, about 52 minutes total. Each piece has a full-choir rehearsal recording (dated, e.g. 'Tue 11 Nov 2026, St. Brendan's Hall, 4:37'), plus learning tracks for soprano, alto, tenor and bass recorded by section leaders (2:10–6:05 long), with bar-number markers at rehearsal letters (A = bar 1, B = bar 17, C = bar 33, D = bar 49). Doreen's saved playback position for each piece, her personal notes ('breathe after "lullay" bar 40'), and a play count per track. The director's note on the piece: 'Altos: bars 33–48, keep the pitch up on the descent.' 3 recordings were added this week by volunteer Marcus Lin.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
